common.visualStyle: Original white2.5D comparisons, forest-green emphasis, separate independent scene for each explanation and gameplay observation.
common.renderer: Existing Manim Community0.20.1 Cairo; preserve the installed series runtime.
common.coordinateConvention: Right-handed column vectors, drawing y-up. Label origin, axes and units before calculating. Changing a source row-vector formula requires an explicit transpose/convention audit.
common.captionSafeArea: Fixed bottom-center boxed-white-forest captions at1920x1080 center(960,970). Keep worked code footers and active equation lines above the tallest two-line caption box.
common.overview: After the original2second cat intro, independently write KO/EN20–30second narration explaining the question, what viewers can calculate, and the actual order of the secured examples.
common.outro: Original10second membership photo/name/badge rows, cat logo and canonical coaching URL.
common.bodyRatio: Measured actual existing-game footage40% / explanation60%, excluding branding and membership; no loops, artificial slow motion, background music or source audio.
common.duration: Aim for focused15–20minute parts. Measure actual narration before deciding whether more splitting is needed; do not cut essential calculations to meet a guessed runtime.
common.developmentFootage: A rendered code illustration is explanation time. No invented game or playable test may fill actual-game time.

parts.centralQuestion: 형태를 계산 가능한 데이터로 바꾸고, 직선·구·상자로 점과 공간을 어떻게 검사할까?

proposedExplanationScenes.claim: The same shape has direct data, a parametric construction and an implicit test.
proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Three equal-sized panels: circle center/radius; moving p(theta)=c+r(cos theta,sin theta); a candidate point changing the sign of ||p-c||²-r². Keep the shape itself consistent across all three.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: An implicit zero set describes the boundary. Interior tests require an inequality and a stated sign.

proposedExplanationScenes.claim: A moved circle needs linear terms in a general quadratic equation.
proposedExplanationScenes.worked: Center(2,3),radius1: (x-2)²+(y-3)²=1 expands to x²+y²-4x-6y+12=0.
proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Slide the circle off the origin, then expand the squares one line at a time. Color the newly introduced x/y terms.

proposedExplanationScenes.claim: A parameter domain determines whether a formula describes a line, ray or segment.
proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Compare t in all real numbers, t>=0 and0<=t<=1 using the same origin/delta arrows.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: Explain the source's finite directed-ray convention separately from the usual infinite ray. A fraction t is not automatically seconds or metres.

proposedExplanationScenes.claim: Unit direction makes a distance parameter meaningful.
proposedExplanationScenes.worked: u=(6,3)/sqrt45, p(s)=origin+s*u. Travel length along the segment is sqrt45.
proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Separate the normalized direction arrow from a ruler labelled in metres; do not use the fraction label on the ruler.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: Zero delta has no unique direction; validate finite coordinates before normalization.

proposedExplanationScenes.claim: Slope/intercept fails for vertical lines; a normal equation still works.
proposedExplanationScenes.worked: Exercise origin(5,3),delta(-7,5): endpoint(-2,8), slope-5/7, intercept46/7. Compare x=1 as a vertical line.
proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Animate two endpoints, rise/run, then n dot p=d; show n perpendicular to the line.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: Only a unit normal makes the residual a signed distance.

proposedExplanationScenes.claim: The normal of an equal-distance bisector points from one endpoint to the other.
proposedExplanationScenes.worked: q=(0,0),r=(2,0), n=(2,0), midpoint(1,0), d=2; the bisector is x=1.
proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Show equal radius segments to an off-axis point(1,2). Compare the incorrect y=0 line through the original points.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: Do not rotate the normal again; coincident q/r do not define a unique bisector.

proposedExplanationScenes.claim: A sphere boundary and a solid ball have different tests.
proposedExplanationScenes.worked: c=(1,2,3),r=2: point(3,2,3) is on the boundary; c is inside; point(4,2,3) is outside.
proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Use a translucent3D sphere with three labelled points; compare squared distances0,4,9 to r²=4.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: Radius must be finite and nonnegative. Use tolerances with units and scale when testing floating-point equality.

proposedExplanationScenes.claim: Radius changes circumference, surface area and volume at different rates.
proposedExplanationScenes.worked: Diameter2r; circle circumference2*pi*r and disk area*pi*r²; sphere surface4*pi*r² and volume4*pi*r³/3.
proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Use separate2D disk and3D sphere panels. Doubling radius highlights factors2,4,8; label length, area and volume units.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: A nonuniformly scaled sphere generally becomes an ellipsoid.

proposedExplanationScenes.claim: An AABB is the intersection of three independent coordinate intervals.
proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Reveal x,y,z slabs before the final box. Keep min/max comparisons in matching axis colors.

proposedExplanationScenes.claim: Construct bounds by comparing each point's coordinates against the matching axis.
proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Distinct syntax/semantic code colors, current point highlighted in the3D plot, active min/max line highlighted in code.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: Define an empty-box state; initialize from the first valid point or infinities; reject nonfinite inputs. Compare y against min.y/max.y and z against min.z/max.z.

proposedExplanationScenes.claim: Overlapping enclosing boxes identify a possible pair, not necessarily touching shapes.
proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Two slender diagonal shapes have overlapping AABBs while remaining separated. Compare sphere, fixed-axis box and oriented box with the same shapes.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: Broadphase needs a later exact/narrowphase decision; visible gameplay does not reveal the actual collider type.

proposedExplanationScenes.claim: Transforming just two opposite corners can miss the new extrema.
proposedExplanationScenes.worked: Rotate a non-square rectangle45degrees. Track all four2D corners first, then extend to eight3D corners.
proposedExplanationScenes.visual: The old min/max pair maps inside the new enclosure; highlight the missed corners in red. Preserve the series' column-vector convention.

proposedExplanationScenes.claim: The center/half-extents method matches an eight-corner enclosure for an affine transform.
proposedExplanationScenes.worked: c'=A*c+t; e'=abs(A)*e; min'=c'-e', max'=c'+e'.
proposedExplanationScenes.visual: One row of A shows how signed coordinate contributions become extent magnitudes. Compare the resulting box with transformed corners.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: This encloses the transformed input box, not generally the tight bounds of the original mesh. Perspective transforms require a different analysis.

proposedExplanationScenes.claim: Bounds of transformed actual points can be tighter than bounds of the transformed whole box.
proposedExplanationScenes.worked: Use the original five points(7,11,-5),(2,3,8),(-3,3,1),(-5,-7,0),(6,3,4). Display audited45degree point bounds beside audited box bounds.
proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Give the five points solid markers and the eight box corners hollow markers. Build the two enclosures independently.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: Separate exact sqrt(.5) from the original rounded .707 coefficient. Retrieve the audited numeric values without silently rounding intermediate calculations.

proposedGameplayConnections.visibleActionRequired: A visible beam/aim line changes with the source or viewing direction and meets an obstruction.
proposedGameplayConnections.viewerFocus: Where the visible path begins, its direction, and the first visible surface it meets.

proposedGameplayConnections.visibleActionRequired: An existing game's clearly rounded object moves in relation to another object or surface.
proposedGameplayConnections.viewerFocus: The observed approximate shape is the motivation for a stated mathematical proxy; never assert a hidden sphere collider.

proposedGameplayConnections.visibleActionRequired: A visible box-like or elongated game object moves or rotates near an opening or obstacle.
proposedGameplayConnections.viewerFocus: Its silhouette spans different world-axis ranges as its orientation changes.

parts.guidedExercise: Compute the ray endpoint and line equation, build bounds of the five source points, then distinguish transformed-box bounds from transformed-point bounds.

parts.centralQuestion: 점이 평면의 어느 쪽에 있는지 계산하고, 삼각형 안의 위치와 속성을 어떻게 보간할까?

proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Compare a plane through the origin with the translated plane y=2.
proposedExplanationScenes.claim: A general plane is an affine set; it need not be a linear subspace through the origin.

proposedExplanationScenes.worked: n=(0,2,0),d=4,p=(4,5,-3): residual6, distance3, closest point(4,2,-3).
proposedExplanationScenes.visual: A perpendicular ruler is distinct from the raw equation residual.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: Normalize n and d together; zero normal is invalid. Distance is (n dot p-d)/||n||.

proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Build two edge vectors from one triangle vertex and reveal their right-handed cross product.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: Point order reverses the normal. Collinear/near-collinear points need validation before dividing by the normal magnitude.

proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Add ordered Newell edge contributions around a polygon, then compare shuffled inputs.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: This is an ordered polygon method, not a general unordered-point least-squares fit.

proposedExplanationScenes.worked: Triangle(0,0),(4,0),(0,3): sides3,4,5; perimeter12; semiperimeter6; area6 by base-height, Heron and cross-product magnitude.
proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Use one triangle across three equal-sized area-method panels.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: Unsigned3D area and signed2D area behave differently under winding reversal.

proposedExplanationScenes.worked: p=lambda1*v1+lambda2*v2+lambda3*v3 with sum(lambda)=1; after choosing v3 as origin, the independent axes are v1-v3 and v2-v3.
proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Vertex, edge midpoint, center and outside points move across the same triangle.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: Nonnegative weights describe points inside/on a nondegenerate triangle. Negative weights are meaningful outside values.

proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Show colored per-vertex contributions before adding the final point; separate weight values from spatial units.
Compare interior signed subareas with an exterior example whose subarea becomes negative.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: Unsigned subareas alone lose the outside signs. The denominator must be nonzero and well-conditioned enough for the required tolerance.

proposedExplanationScenes.worked: Query(1.8,2,7) has the same XY projection as the inside example but lies7units off the plane.
proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Use linked3D and2D views; the projected point stays fixed while z increases.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: Dropping the largest-normal-component axis helps solve projected coordinates; it does not prove that the original query is on the plane.

proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Use the same three weights to mix three vertex colors or another explicitly defined scalar attribute.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: Attribute interpolation is a mathematical explanation. Do not classify this animated triangle as actual-game footage or silently substitute screen-space affine weights for perspective-correct rasterization.

proposedGameplayConnections.visibleActionRequired: A character/object moves above and below, or approaches, a clearly visible reference surface.
proposedGameplayConnections.viewerFocus: The visible side of the surface and perpendicular separation, rather than an unobserved infinite in-game plane.

proposedGameplayConnections.visibleActionRequired: Actual interaction with a game surface or a visibly triangular region.
proposedGameplayConnections.viewerFocus: A location relative to three explicitly chosen reference points; no assertion about the game's hidden mesh indices or shading implementation.

parts.guidedExercise: Normalize the plane correctly, compute signed distance, reconstruct a point from three weights, and reject the off-plane query even though its projection matches.

parts.centralQuestion: 삼각형의 서로 다른 중심을 구분하고, 다각형을 유효한 삼각형들로 어떻게 나눌까?

proposedExplanationScenes.worked: Triangle(0,0),(4,0),(0,3): centroid(4/3,1), incenter(1,1), circumcenter(2,1.5).
proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Reveal medians, angle bisectors and perpendicular bisectors independently before comparing the three centers.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: A uniform triangular lamina has the centroid at the vertex average. A game's arbitrary mass distribution need not.

proposedExplanationScenes.worked: Weight each vertex by the opposite side length(5,3,4); perimeter12, area6; r=2A/perimeter=1.
proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Draw the inscribed circle and three perpendicular equal-distance segments.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: Do not omit the factor2 when using the full perimeter.

proposedExplanationScenes.worked: Right triangle circumradius2.5. Obtuse triangle(0,0),(4,0),(1,1) has circumcenter(2,-1), outside the triangle.
proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Vary the angle through acute/right/obtuse; show equal vertex distances, not equal edge distances.
Compare a simple ordered contour, a contour with a hole and a self-intersecting contour.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: Finite coordinates, repeated vertices, zero-length edges, collinearity, planarity and self-intersections are separate checks. State library-specific simple/complex terminology.

proposedExplanationScenes.visual: A segment between two interior points remains inside a convex polygon; a concave notch provides a counterexample.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: Same-sign turn tests assume a valid simple ordered contour. Convexity alone does not prove planarity or simplicity.

proposedExplanationScenes.worked: A valid convex polygon with7vertices produces7-2=5 fan triangles.
proposedExplanationScenes.visual: Reveal one diagonal and triangle at a time, preserving contour winding and shared vertices.
Show the outside fan triangle. Compare the audited signed area sum with the larger sum of absolute triangle areas.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: Signed area cancellation can equal the polygon area even when the fan is not a valid partition.

proposedExplanationScenes.visual: On the audited simple L-shaped contour, remove ears1,2,3 and keep the final triangle. Reveal four nonoverlapping triangles with areas2,1.5,1.5,2, totaling7.
proposedExplanationScenes.guard: The independent audit checks convex ears, other-vertex exclusion and2021 nonboundary coverage samples for this example. It does not validate a general triangulation implementation or hole handling. A quality heuristic or arbitrary fan does not solve every contour.

proposedGameplayConnections.visibleActionRequired: An actual triangular game structure or chosen three-point reference arrangement.
proposedGameplayConnections.viewerFocus: Each center answers a different geometric question; the visual structure is not evidence of a hidden physical center of mass.

proposedGameplayConnections.visibleActionRequired: A visible convex/concave boundary or placement path in an existing game.
proposedGameplayConnections.viewerFocus: A notch, diagonal or crossing that can be directly seen, without asserting unobserved triangulation/collision decomposition.

parts.guidedExercise: Calculate the three centers of the3-4-5 triangle, count a seven-vertex convex fan, then explain why the concave fan fails.
